QuestionStmt.S: The solubility of AgBr is $7.1 \times 10^{-7}$ mol dm⁻³. Calculate its solubility product at the same temperature.

Solution.S:
AgBr dissociates as: AgBr(s) ⇌ Ag⁺(aq) + Br⁻(aq).

If solubility is S = 7.1 × 10⁻⁷ mol/dm³, then [Ag⁺] = S and [Br⁻] = S.

Ksp = [Ag⁺][Br⁻] = S × S = S² = (7.1 × 10⁻⁷)² = 5.04 × 10⁻¹³.

Thus the correct option is D: 5.04 × 10⁻¹³.
